open_points.subject: store capability failure handling
open_points.text: “a store call that fails changes no record ... and the request is answered as an internal error by module:surface — except the removal of a run's spool” contradicts “store.spool_file alone checks both ceilings ... and on a refusal keeps nothing” and the flows that classify that refusal as resource_exhausted or contract_violation.
open_points.question: Which unsuccessful store results are expected domain refusals with their stated outcomes, and which are internal errors that stop the kernel?
options: Treat ceiling and unavailable-byte refusals as domain outcomes; reserve internal_error for unexpected store failures
Treat every unsuccessful store call except spool removal as internal_error
Define the classification separately for each store capability
open_points.default_guess: Treat documented refusals such as spool ceilings and unavailable spool bytes as domain outcomes, and only unexpected persistence failures as internal_error.

open_points.subject: bindings.check_installed_instances at startup
open_points.text: “a manifest record that cannot be read or fails a check of the record itself (A08 rule 5) stops the start naming it” does not identify an operation or proposal ports, although A08 rule 5 includes operation-specific effect-class, route, idempotency-key and proposed-port checks.
open_points.question: Exactly which manifest checks must check_installed_instances perform at startup when it has no operation name or proposed ports?
options: Check only service/selected-instance facts needed to detect credential-header collisions
Validate every capability entry using only checks that do not require proposal ports
Require additional operation and port inputs for the startup check
open_points.default_guess: Check only the manifest and selected-instance facts needed for credential-header collision detection; leave operation-specific checks to proposal, acceptance and send.
